task: Push GPT Astra web-UI assessment task to Kaggle benchmarks (cokro-web-ui-assessment) as a server-side benchmark task
what_went_wrong: Push of task version 1 validated as Kernel_Without_Run: 'Your task notebook completed but did not produce any run output.' Kernel log showed the real error: kbench failed to store Run #1 - 'utf-8 codec can't encode characters in position 35959-35960: surrogates not allowed' in the conversations/requests/contents/parts/text field. The task body itself had run (registry printed, gpt-6-astra selected, DONE printed) but the run record was rejected, so no run was registered and `tasks run` refused ('Only completed tasks can be run'). The likely API call from v1 was consumed with no retrievable output (wasted ~$0.29 of Astra quota).
root_cause: The builder embedded the frontend source bundle as SOURCE = <json.dumps(bundle)> (pattern copied from the prior session's build_kala.py). The web source contains 5 astral chars (emoji U+1FA7A, U+1F4AC, U+1F52C in ask/content.tsx; U+1F44D, U+1F44E in answer/content.tsx). json.dumps escapes astral chars as surrogate-PAIR escapes (\ud83d\ude00). Python STRING LITERALS parse those escapes as TWO LONE surrogates (Python does not recombine surrogate pairs - unlike json.loads, which does). The resulting SOURCE str held lone surrogates at parsed position 33463+; the prompt preamble offset (+~2500) lands at ~35959 - an exact match with the reported failing position. kbench's run serializer utf-8-encodes the conversation text, which rejects lone surrogates, so the whole run record failed to store. build_kala.py never hit this because its kala.txt contained only BMP non-ASCII (em-dashes), which parse cleanly from \u2014 escapes.
what_i_actually_did_wrong: Reused the proven embedding pattern from build_kala.py without auditing the NEW content for astral characters, and did not pre-verify that the generated task file's SOURCE literal parses surrogate-free. Diagnosed only after the first push failed, via kernel log download (kaggle kernels output) - the CLI's status message alone was a dead end.
fix: Builder now strips chars > 0xFFFF ('?' placeholder) from the bundle before json.dumps and asserts none remain. Verified the rebuilt task file: syntax OK, 0 surrogate escapes anywhere in file, module-level SOURCE literal eval-parses to 123,365 chars with 0 lone surrogates. Re-pushed as version 2 -> status Completed -> `tasks run -m gpt-6-astra --wait` -> COMPLETED -> report downloaded (23,174 chars, 3/3 assertions PASSED, cost $0.29326).
lesson: Embedding external text into generated Python via json.dumps is surrogate-safe ONLY for BMP content. Always verify by eval-parsing the literal as Python source (NOT json.loads - that would falsely pass by recombining pairs) and asserting no U+D800-U+DFFF code units remain. Also: when kaggle benchmarks task status shows an opaque error, fetch the validation kernel's log with `kaggle kernels output <ref>` - it contains the actual Python error.
